statsResetConfirmationMessage: Are you sure you want to delete all player statistics? This action cannot be undone.
rulesGoalText: Move all 15 of your checkers across the board and bear them off before your opponent.
rulesMovementText:
• All checkers start at the starting point ('head').
• White and black checkers move counter-clockwise along their routes.
• A checker can only be placed on an empty point or a point occupied by your own checkers.
• Placing a checker on a point occupied by even one opponent's checker is not allowed.
rulesDiceText:
• At the start of the turn, the player rolls two dice.
• The rolled values determine the number of points to move.
• You can make two separate moves or one move for the sum of the dice values.
• If a double is rolled, each value is played four times.
• If only one move is possible, the player is obliged to make it.
• If no move is possible, the turn is skipped.
rulesHeadText:
• Only one checker can be taken from the head per turn.
• Exception: on the first turn of the game, if a double 3-3, 4-4, or 6-6 is rolled, you can take two checkers.
rulesBlockText:
• A player can occupy consecutive points with their checkers, creating blocks.
• It is forbidden to build a continuous block of six points in a row if there are no opponent's checkers ahead of the block.
rulesHomeText:
• The last six points of the route form the player's home.
• After all 15 checkers have entered the home, they can be borne off the board.
• The number on the die allows bearing off a checker from the corresponding point.
• If there is no checker on the required point, you can bear off a checker from the nearest higher point.
rulesVictoryText:
• Oin (1 point): The opponent bore off at least one checker.
• Mars (2 points): The opponent did not bear off any checkers.
• Home Mars (3 points): The opponent did not bear off any checkers and did not get all their checkers into their own home.
rulesTipText: Try not only to move your checkers forward but also to create obstacles for your opponent. Well-constructed blocks often decide the outcome of the game sooner than lucky dice rolls.
